profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility LAX12, at 2260 East El Segundo Boulevard, El Segundo, CA 90245. Digital Realty's own property listing for LAX12, fetched this session, lists the building at 129,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Los Angeles metro footprint, concentrated in El Segundo near Los Angeles International Airport, a historic hub for submarine cable landing stations and carrier interconnection on the US West Coast, alongside a downtown Los Angeles building at 600 West 7th Street also in the company's portfolio. Digital Realty markets its Los Angeles properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Silicon Valley, Northern Virginia, Dallas, Chicago, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and Southern California Edison serve most of the greater LA data center market depending on jurisdiction.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage; the company reports its portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than disclosing per-building IT power ratings for any of its facilities, a pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched this session, not specific to this building alone.

reading.body:
DRT LAX12 is a 129,000 square foot colocation facility in El Segundo operated by Digital Realty, a wholesale landlord that does not publish IT power ratings for individual buildings. Digital Realty's own specification pages and SEC filings disclose aggregate metrics by region and metro rather than per-facility megawatts, so the power capacity of this building is not publicly stated. Without a published power figure, it is impossible to estimate the scale of compute this campus can host or compare it directly to other AI training facilities.

This facility is one of two named Digital Realty properties in the Los Angeles metro area serving the broader Southern California market via the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and Southern California Edison. It sits in El Segundo near Los Angeles International Airport, a long-established hub for submarine cable landings and carrier interconnection on the US West Coast. Digital Realty positions its LA properties alongside Silicon Valley, Northern Virginia, and Dallas within its PlatformDIGITAL colocation network, but LA is a smaller metro footprint for the company compared to its densest hubs.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities across the state, with only 11 publishing megawatt figures totaling 365 MW of disclosed capacity. This building ranks 12th in published megawatts for the state, but that ranking reflects the unpublished denominator: most California facilities, including this one, do not disclose power capacity in any public source this registry has found. Without that data, whether DRT LAX12 matters to AI scaling cannot be determined from available facts.
